result.stdout:
feedfence check [path] [options]
feedfence --help
feedfence --version

Checks already-restored package IDs against effective NuGet source policy.
Package IDs use NuGet's normal package-ID validation; unsafe or malformed identities fail closed.
Declared dependency targets must use supported NuGet values and compatible assets records.
Requires the last restore's obj/<project-file-name>.nuget.dgspec.json evaluated inputs.
Checks selected-root/framework dependency flow, including private child edges.
Incomplete dependency closure or solution membership fails with exit 2 and no partial report.
FF006 reports enabled HTTP sources and disabled TLS certificate validation.
FF003 reports no eligible mapped source, including zero enabled sources when mapping is active.
Missing user settings without a packageSources clear require initialization or --config.
Policy discovery searches logical and physical target ancestors through .git, or the filesystem root without Git.
Directory inputs resolve a target first; project/solution file aliases retain both ancestry views.
Absent policy is optional; multiple ancestor policies are ambiguous and fail with exit 2.
Implicit policy must be a readable regular file inside the physical repository boundary.
Only directory or regular-file .git markers bound discovery; other object types exit 2.
Policy FIFOs, sockets and devices are rejected before opening, including explicit overrides.
Policy and report contract: https://github.com/KeelMatrix/FeedFence/blob/main/docs/report-contract.md
All policy links and ancestors resolve before repository ownership is checked.
Conflicting ancestry or a target redirected outside its implicit policy repository exits 2.
Unusable policy paths or discovery failures exit 2 with no report in every format.
FeedFence never restores packages or contacts package feeds during analysis.

Options:
  --config <path>  Use this NuGet configuration instead of hierarchy discovery.
                   NuGet's implicit machine defaults still apply and are bounded before parsing
[truncated]
